recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not reintroduce DiagnosticOrder- or DAF-specific edits in core; handle any future reason/supportingInfo changes under their own ServiceRequest trackers rather than this superseded note-cardinality issue.
issue_request: FHIR-8147 was Published with a Persuasive disposition for DSTU1. It asked that DiagnosticOrder.clinicalNotes support multiple notes instead of a single string field, with the OO resolution directing the base resource change to DiagnosticOrder.note 0..* using Annotation in coordination with FHIR-7622.
initial_application: No git commit explicitly mentions FHIR-8147 in its subject. The related pre-application commit a7b323be06, titled "pre-applied #7134,#7135,#7684", replaced DiagnosticOrder.clinicalNotes with reason/supportingInformation handling and added DiagnosticOrder.note as 0..* Annotation; the current ServiceRequest.note source still carries a committee note referencing 7134 and 8147.
additional_context: DiagnosticOrder was renamed to DiagnosticRequest and later subsumed into ServiceRequest. source/fhir.ini actively lists ServiceRequest as the current resource, comments that DiagnosticOrder was subsumed into ServiceRequest, and maps ServiceRequest.notes to ServiceRequest.note. FHIR-7622, the broader Annotation guidance cited by FHIR-8147, is already represented on the combined branch by an Issue-Reconcile-Key: FHIR-7622 no-change audit commit. Current source contains no DiagnosticOrder.clinicalNotes or DiagnosticRequest.clinicalNotes target left to fix, and the old DAF guide/profile paths are not present in the current build.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The active current source already satisfies the seed because ServiceRequest.note is 0..* Annotation and carries the historical FHIR-8147 committee-note reference, while obsolete DiagnosticOrder/DiagnosticRequest and DAF profile locations are outside the current build.
